date: Mecca, about 602 — the Conquest of Mecca, 8 AH (630)
title: 101cw1t
Who is Mu'awiya? His family, Abu Sufyan, Hind and Hamza
hook: Mu'awiya is the son of a house that drew the sword against the Prophet. At Uhud Hamza's liver was chewed in that house.
scenes.0.text: **Mu'awiya** was born in Mecca, in the Umayyad branch of the Quraysh. His father is **Abu Sufyan**, his mother **Hind bint Utba**. This family was among the houses that most harshly opposed the Prophet's call. In later years the dynasty that stood against the ==Ahl al-Bayt== came from this house.
scenes.1.text: At **Badr**, **Uhud** and the **Trench**, **Abu Sufyan** was at the head of the polytheist army. He drove the army against the Prophet. He stood at the head of enmity to Islam. This war did not stop until Mecca was conquered.
scenes.2.text: At **Badr** **Hind**'s father, brother and uncle died. She carried this grudge to **Uhud**. She promised Wahshi freedom and a reward so that he would kill **Hamza**. Wahshi martyred the Prophet's uncle with a spear. That day Mecca took its revenge on the ==Ahl al-Bayt==.
scenes.3.text: At Uhud **Hind** mutilated **Hamza**'s body. She ==chewed his liver.== She made a necklace from his ears and nose. The Prophet felt deep pain on seeing his uncle in this state. This savagery is the view of Islam held by the house **Mu'awiya** was born into. The lovers remember that day by the Prophet's weeping.
scenes.4.text: When Mecca was conquered, **Abu Sufyan**'s war ended. The Prophet gave amnesty, saying, "Whoever enters Abu Sufyan's house is safe." He and **Hind** appeared Muslim that day. In the Shia reading, this was not a surrender from the heart but an appearance forced by the conquest. The man who had led armies for years said the word when his life and house were in danger. The word here is the kalimat al-shahada. It means I am a Muslim.
scenes.5.text: The year of the conquest is 8 AH. **Mu'awiya** also appeared Muslim that year. In the Hunayn spoils he was placed with his father among those whose hearts were to be won over. This share is remembered not as love but as spoils given to new arrivals. After this house took that share it still did not stop standing against the ==Ahl al-Bayt==.
scenes.6.text: At this time it is related that the Prophet said of **Mu'awiya**, "May God not fill his belly." In the Shia reading this is not a compliment but a warning. The claim of his being a scribe also pales beside this saying. The one said to have held the pen later had **Imam Ali** cursed from the pulpits.
scenes.7.text: This house that led armies against the Prophet in Mecca appeared Muslim with the conquest. Then it became the most powerful dynasty. **Imam Ali** was cursed from the pulpits. **Imam Hasan**'s peace was trampled. **Imam Husayn**'s road led to **Yazid**. It is remembered with what was done to **Hamza** at Uhud. At Karbala too, the same house caused thirst.
sunni.0.says: Wahshi killing Hamza with a spear at Uhud.
sunni.1.says: The Prophet granting amnesty to everyone who enters Abu Sufyan's house.
sunni.2.says: The Prophet's saying about Mu'awiya, «May God not fill his belly», and the commentators' interpretation.
sunni.3.says: What Hind did to Hamza's body and the situation after Uhud.
shia.0.says: Abu Sufyan's enmity, Hind's role at Uhud, and the discussion of the characterization of Mu'awiya as a scribe.
disputes.0.title: 1q94d7o
His becoming Muslim and the scribeship
disputes.0.sunni: That Mu'awiya became Muslim with the conquest is told in the sources. In the Sunni reading he is a Companion and one of the Prophet's scribes; his earlier family background does not change his later ruling.
disputes.0.shia: That Mu'awiya became Muslim with the conquest is told in the sources. In the Shia account he is counted among those who professed faith while their lives were in danger; sincerity is assessed together with his later conduct.
disputes.1.title: 1qtjukm
Hamza and Hind
disputes.1.sunni: That Hamza was martyred at Uhud is told in both traditions. In the Sunni reading Hind later became Muslim and the Prophet forgave her.
disputes.1.shia: That Hamza was martyred at Uhud is told in both traditions. In the Shia account this pain is remembered as part of the family's earlier stance toward the Prophet.
questions.0: When Mu'awiya's family had fought against the Prophet, what does it make you think that they later took part in government?
questions.1: How much does a person's family background before becoming Muslim help you in understanding his later path?
questions.2: The saying about Mu'awiya in Muslim can be heard differently in different hearts. When reading a text, what do love and caution tell you?
summary: Mu'awiya is the son of Abu Sufyan and Hind, who stood against Islam in Mecca. The martyrdom of Hamza at Uhud is part of this family's past with the Prophet. The family became Muslim with the conquest. His being counted a scribe appears in Sunni books; in the Shia account it is disputed.
key: Hamza at Uhud and the family that became Muslim with the conquest
notes.0: Mu'awiya is the son of Abu Sufyan b. Harb and Hind bint Utba.
notes.1: Abu Sufyan was at the head of the polytheist army at Uhud and the Trench.
notes.2: Hind is remembered for what she did to Hamza's body at Uhud (sira sources).
notes.3: The family became Muslim at the conquest of Mecca (8 AH).
notes.4: It is related that the Prophet said, «May God not fill his belly».
